delete.heading: Delete {{name}}
delete.note_one: It's deleted {{days}} days after you ask, and any owner can keep it until then. On that day its {{n}} person loses access and is signed out.
delete.note_other: It's deleted {{days}} days after you ask, and any owner can keep it until then. On that day its {{n}} people lose access and are signed out.

delete.confirmDescription_other: It's deleted on {{date}}, {{days}} days from now. Until then it works as usual, and any owner can keep it. On that day its {{n}} people lose access and are signed out.

delete.scheduledDescription_other: Until then it works as usual. On that day its {{n}} people lose access and are signed out. Any owner can keep it until then.

details.description: How {{name}} appears to the people in it.

about.slugHint: Its unique short name, set when {{name}} was created. It can't be changed.
about.regionHint: Chosen when {{name}} was created. It can't be changed.
about.idHint: Use it in the API, or quote it to support.

domains.title: Domains
domains.description: Prove {{name}} owns its email domains, and choose the address its people sign in at.

email.title: Email domains
email.description: {{name}} manages the accounts on a domain it verifies: its single sign-on and directories can create them there, and no other organisation can.
email.noneLine: Verify one, and {{name}} manages the accounts on it.
email.noAccess: Seeing this organisation's domains needs permission to read its connections.

row.pending: Waiting for its TXT record to be checked

failure.notFound: The last check didn't find its TXT record.
failure.lookup: The last check couldn't look up its DNS.

panel.verified: Verified {{date}} with the TXT record below. {{name}} manages the accounts on @{{domain}} and the domains under it.
panel.pending: Publish this TXT record at your DNS provider, then check it. Qeet ID checks only when you ask.

panel.recordVerified: Qeet ID checked it once, when the domain was verified.

remove.title: Remove {{domain}}?
remove.descriptionVerified: {{name}} stops managing the accounts on @{{domain}}: its single sign-on and directories can't create new ones there, and other organisations can. People who already have accounts keep them.
remove.descriptionPending: {{domain}} isn't verified, so no one's account changes. To verify it later, add it again and publish its new record.

add.title: Add a domain
add.description: Next, you'll publish a TXT record at your DNS provider to prove {{name}} owns it.
add.label: Domain
add.hint: The part after the @ in your people's email addresses.
add.invalid: Enter a domain, such as qeet.co.in.

address.noAccess: Seeing the sign-in address needs permission to read this organisation's connections.

security.title: Security
security.description: The sign-in rules for everyone in {{name}}. Your own two-step verification is in <account>My account</account>.

mfa.title: Two-step verification
mfa.description: Whether people need a second step when they sign in. Someone an administrator marks as needing one must use it whatever this says.

value.optional: No one: only people who set one up

mfa.coverage: {{n}} of {{total}} people have set one up.
mfa.graceRunning: Turned on {{since}}; people who were members then have until {{until}} to set one up.
mfa.editDescription: Anyone who needs it and has none sets one up when they next sign in, or once their days run out.

choice.required: Everyone sets one up before they get in.
choice.requiredCount_one: Everyone sets one up before they get in: {{count}} person hasn't yet.
choice.requiredCount_other: Everyone sets one up before they get in: {{count}} people haven't yet.
choice.admin_only: People whose roles let them change anything must use one; others may.
choice.optional: Only people who set one up are asked for it.

mfa.daysHint: For people who were members when it was turned on: until then they can sign in without one, and 0 asks them at their next sign-in. New members set one up at their first.

passwords.title: Passwords
passwords.description: The rules a password must meet are set, and enforced, in Sign-in › Password.
passwords.lineUnknown: Its length, and the characters it needs
passwords.off: Passwords are turned off: people sign in another way.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.description: Changes apply to sessions that start after them; open ones keep the lifetime they started with.
sessions.maxAgeHint: However active they are, people sign in again after this, in apps too.
sessions.idleHint: A session unused for this long ends. It can't outlast the longest session.
sessions.perPersonHint: How many places one person can be signed in at once.
sessions.atLimitEvict: At the limit, a new sign-in ends their least recently used session.
sessions.atLimitRefuse: At the limit, a new sign-in is refused.
sessions.limitDescription: A limit on the sessions each person has open at once.
sessions.limitHint: From 1 to 1,000. Leave it empty for no limit.
sessions.evict: End their least recently used session

stepUp.title: Confirming sensitive actions
stepUp.description: Before changing factors, keys, secrets, sign-in settings or roles, people confirm with a second step again.
stepUp.windowHint: In the session it was made in; signing out ends it.
stepUp.factorsDescription: A second step with any of these confirms a sensitive action. At least one stays.

network.title: Network access
network.line: Which networks can sign in to {{name}} is set by its IP rules.
